actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository provides three manipulation tasks - push, slide and pick-and-place - for the Franka Emika Panda arm, implemented on the MuJoCo physics engine
The pick-and-place environment loads its scene from assets/pick_and_place.xml
The scene includes the robot model panda_mocap.xml from the same directory
The scene sets the integrator to Euler, noslip_iterations to 3, the timestep to 0.002 s and the cone to pyramidal
The scene compiles with the radian angle unit, the ./meshes/ mesh directory and automatic limits
The scene adds a free object body at (0.4, 0, 0.2) whose box geom has mass 0.1 and size 0.02 m, and a target site at the same position
The robot model declares the seven arm joints joint1 to joint7
The default class panda gives every arm joint armature 0.1, damping 1, axis 0 0 1 and the range -2.8973 to 2.8973 rad, and its actuators the ctrlrange -2.8973 to 2.8973 and forcerange -87 to 87
The default class finger gives the gripper finger joints a slide joint on axis 0 1 0 with the range 0 to 0.04 m
The two actuator sections declare seven general actuators for the arm joints and two for the gripper fingers, and the finger actuators have the ctrlrange 0 to 0.04
The robot model welds the mocap body panda_mocap to the end-effector body ee_center_body, so the end effector is driven by a mocap pose and not by joint position commands
The environment states that the model has 9 actuators (7 arm and 2 gripper joints), 16 generalized coordinates (9 arm and gripper plus the 7 of the object's free joint) and 15 degrees of freedom
The environment takes its control range from the model's actuator_ctrlrange
The environment action is three Cartesian displacements plus a gripper command unless the gripper is blocked
The pick-and-place environment runs 25 physics substeps per step, uses the distance threshold 0.05 and samples the object and the goal in a 0.3 m range with a 0.2 m height range
The package registers the three tasks, each with a sparse and a dense reward, with 50 steps per episode
A step clips the action to the action-space bounds and runs ten physics steps of n_substeps each

determinism.notes: the carried model and a fixed control sequence are deterministic in the MuJoCo engine, but a real engine run was never made here and the bridge's seed is only recorded; the stand-in state is deterministic

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in mujoco module, not the MuJoCo engine: it parses the integration step, the joint counts and the actuator ctrlranges of model.xml and panda_mocap.xml and advances time (every qpos follows its qvel, which stays zero); it computes no equations of motion, contacts, mocap welds or actuator dynamics, so a ctrl vector changes nothing but data.ctrl

the package carries the two XML files only (model.xml and panda_mocap.xml); the 33 MB of meshes the scene references through meshdir ./meshes/ are not carried, so a real MuJoCo load needs that assets directory beside model.xml

the clone's environments are MuJoCoRobotEnv subclasses of a reinforcement-learning library with observations, rewards, a mocap-driven end effector and goal sampling (panda_mujoco_gym/envs/panda_env.py); this package serves the raw model, not those environments, and that library is not carried
the model drives the end effector through the mocap weld; a ctrl vector moves the arm joints, which the environment's own action mode does not use
snapshot and restore use the bridge's copied time/qpos/qvel/ctrl fallback, not mjSTATE_INTEGRATION
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model's timestep only
the model was never validated against a physical Franka arm

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the world state stays readable
